_about: How the email lens reads a footprint's mail records. For each registered domain it reads the mail servers (dns.json mail_rr_types), the SPF policy (a TXT record of the domain starting with spf_prefix, RFC 7208), the DMARC policy (a TXT record of the dmarc_label name below the domain starting with dmarc_prefix, RFC 7489) and the DKIM keys stored for names below the dkim_label name (RFC 6376). SPF ending in one of permissive_all lets anyone send as the domain; softfail_all only marks such mail. A DMARC policy in monitor_policies asks receivers to deliver spoofed mail anyway. A domain that receives no mail should still publish an SPF policy of none_spf and a DMARC policy of reject so that it cannot be spoofed. Records are only as complete as the enumeration: a DMARC name that was never queried reads as none stored. Add values here, not in Go code. mail_providers name who receives a domain's mail from its MX hosts: pattern is a regular expression matched, ignoring case, against the whole MX host name, and source is the provider's own documentation of the MX hosts its customers use. A host no pattern matches is named by its registrable domain. Add providers here, not in Go code, and only with such a source. policy_providers name the shared mail-policy providers whose own domains appear in many unrelated domains' SPF includes or DMARC reporting addresses; the horizontal spf-authorizes and dmarc-reports-to signals skip one so a provider's domain is not read as common ownership. pattern is a regular expression matched, ignoring case, against the referenced domain; source is the provider's own documentation. This is secondary to the per-target fanout cap, which already skips a domain referenced by many apexes; add providers here, not in Go code, and only with such a source.
